facility_roles.quote: It operates in the Antiproton Decelerator (AD) Hall, using antiprotons slowed down by the ELENA facility.

intervals.label: approved by the CERN Research Board
intervals.quote: GBAR was approved by the CERN Research Board in May 2012 and received its first beam of antiprotons from ELENA in October 2018.

intervals.label: commissioning on ELENA
intervals.note: End: "At the end of 2022 ... the GBAR collaboration detected some 20 antihydrogen atoms produced in this way" (CERN, 14 July 2023); the exact day is not stated.
intervals.quote: GBAR was approved by the CERN Research Board in May 2012 and received its first beam of antiprotons from ELENA in October 2018.

intervals.label: antihydrogen production and measurement preparation
intervals.note: Start is the end-2022 antihydrogen run. End: 31 August 2026 (LS3).
intervals.quote: At the end of 2022, during an operation that lasted several days, the GBAR collaboration detected some 20 antihydrogen atoms produced in this way, validating this "in-flight" production method for the first time.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 (no antiproton beam)
intervals.note: The Antimatter Factory (AD and ELENA) delivered its last beams on 31 August 2026 and "will progressively return to operation from 2028 onwards, with the different injectors and facilities restarting in stages" (CERN, 31 August 2026); no experiment-specific restart date is published, so the end is left open.
intervals.quote: CERN’s injector complex and Antimatter Factory took their final steps towards Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) this morning, as the last particle beams were extracted and the machines fell silent.

physics_goals.quote: By measuring the acceleration of antihydrogen under gravity and comparing it with the acceleration of regular hydrogen, GBAR scientists can look for differences in the behaviour of matter and antimatter.
physics_goals.value: Measure the freefall acceleration of antihydrogen under gravity and compare it with that of hydrogen to test the equivalence principle

summary.plain: A CERN experiment designed to let single antihydrogen atoms fall about 20 centimetres and record where they annihilate, comparing the fall with that of ordinary hydrogen. Its first antihydrogen atoms were made at the end of 2022.
summary.technical: GBAR (Gravitational Behaviour of Antihydrogen at Rest): antihydrogen ions made by charge exchange with positronium from a linac positron source, sympathetically cooled to microkelvin temperatures and neutralised for a free-fall measurement. First beam from ELENA October 2018; first antihydrogen end 2022.
